la:adv:mecum.html:
mēcum, i. e. cum me,
with me, like tecum, secum, etc., v. ego.

la:adj:mechanicus.html:
mēchănĭcus, a, um, adj., = μηχανικός,
of or belonging to mechanics, mechanical (ante-class. and post-Aug.).
Adj.: disciplina,: opera,: ars, Firm. Math. 6, 31.—
Subst.
mēchănĭcus, i, m., a mechanic, Lucil. ap. Fest. s. v. petauristas, p. 206 Müll.: sipho, quem diabeten vocant mechanici,; .—
mē-chănĭca, ae, f., mechanics: Cyriades mechanicae professor,.—
mēchănĭca, ōrum, n., works of mechanical art, .
